_comment: How the objects inventoried from the footage (eco-video/objects_from_video.json) become objects of the map. Rules are tried in order; the first whose room (or '*'), kind (optional) and regex `match` on the label (or `hint` on the position hint) fit takes the object; several shots that match one rule are merged into one object (all timestamps kept as sightings, titles merged, count = max). Positions are room-local metres (x to the right, z downwards on the plan); `anchor` places the object in front of a bookcase (`dist` metres from its face, `along` metres from its centre, `on_top` on its top board), on/near another object of this file (`object`, `offset`, `on_top`), or on a wall (`wall` N/E/S/W, `at` metres along it, `dist` from it). `attach` records the sighting on a bookcase instead of drawing an object (cabinet contents, shelf labels, books lying flat). `skip` drops it (ceilings, radiators, footage of other places). `walls` lists the consolidated wall ids (books_by_wall_eco.json, without the video prefix) whose pile readings belong to this object; an entry may be an object {"wall": id, "raw_from": s, "raw_to": s} limited to a window of the reader's raw seconds, so one reader's wall can feed two piles of the same piece of furniture; with `defer: true` the entry is only a fallback: a consolidated book read on that wall is placed by its sightings on other (non-deferred) walls and comes here only when it has none (the salotto piano: the old 'study-desk-piles-1' pass is deferred to the twelve per-pile walls salotto-piano-pile-NN). An object anchor may give `along_frac` (0 = the carrying object's left end as seen from its front, 1 = its right end) instead of, or on top of, an `offset` along its width; `dims_m` [w, d, h] on a rule is copied to the object; `crop` is the thumbnail window of its best frame. `position_hint`, `books_high`, `thumb_frame` and `thumb_raw_s` on the piano pile rules document the placement and are not read by the generator. The object's room wins over the reader's room label: a pile read from a frame belongs to the pile the inventory places, never to a shelf as well. `shape` is a hint for the page (box, cylinder, sphere, torus, flat, stand, lute). Unmatched objects are placed automatically from their position hint.
